latest_releases.title: AOS 7.3.0.1
latest_releases.summary: AOS 7.3.0.1 is here — a refinement release that polishes your experience with improved stability, sharper compatibility, and critical bug fixes. It’s everything you love about AOS, made even smoother. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. 🌟 What’s New One Small Fix. One Giant Leap for Stability. Resolved a rare but critical issue that caused Stargate and Curator services to fail on deduplication-enabled clusters after upgrading to AOS 7.3. ⚙️ Bundled Software AOS 7.3.0.1 ships with: NCC 5.2.0 NGT 4.3 Foundation 5.9 LCM 3.2 Flow Network Security 4.2.1 🛠️ Resolved Issues — Fast. Reliable. Resilient. 🔧 Stargate stability restored. Previously, enabling deduplication could crash key services — now resolved. 🚧 Known Issues — Heads-Up So You’re a Step Ahead AHV Management Post-upgrade, cluster CPU features may downgrade NIC deployment errors using v4 API Flash mode toggle may fail with volume groups Data Replication & Protection Force delete tasks may hang Snapshot replication quirks with NearSync Manual VM recovery may omit NIC Prism & NGT Web console may fail under high load NGT service may fail post-upgrade Infrastructure & Services On-disk deduplication may auto-disable on large fresh deployments VM memory changes round up on AHV Networking Virtual switch updates may fail if launched from Prism Central 📦 Upgrade Essentials Use Life Cycle Manager (LCM) via Prism to upgrade. V3 VM APIs are not supported in Prism Element. Stick with Prism Central. Host-based reservation is deprecated —switch to segment-based. VLAN Discovery is disabled by default for safety. Compatibility with NetBackup 8.2 requires an EEB from Veritas. ✅ Feature Support by Hypervisor Whether you're running AHV, ESXi, or Hyper-V, AOS 7.3.0.1 brings robust support across critical features like: Self-service restore Async DR with NearSync VM roles and RBAC vGPU, vNUMA, and whole-node maintenance mode (For full compatibility, check the matrix in the Support Portal ).

latest_releases.title: Nutanix Enterprise AI 2.4
latest_releases.summary: A powerful step forward in performance, control, and simplicity. Nutanix Enterprise AI 2.4 introduces meaningful improvements that make managing inference endpoints faster, smarter, and more flexible—across edge, on-prem, or cloud environments. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. 🧠 Smarter Performance, Built-In CPU and GPU Acceleration Choose between GPU or Intel® AMX-enabled CPU acceleration for optimal performance—tailored to your workload. Expanded Model Support Pre-validated support for new Hugging Face and NVIDIA models including Llama 3 , Mistral , Stable Diffusion , and more. Now with NVIDIA H200 GPU support Tap into the next generation of high-performance AI acceleration. 🛠️ A Simpler, Smoother Workflow New Endpoint Creation Wizard A guided, intuitive flow for building endpoints—no YAML needed. Create Endpoints from Imported Models Go from model import to deployment in a single click. Auto Model Size Detection Model size is now automatically detected when importing from Hugging Face. HTTP Proxy Support Easily connect to external services—even from air-gapped or dark sites. 🔐 More Control, More Confidence Fine-Grained Access to Models Control exactly which models your users can import or upload—via catalog, direct URLs, or manual upload. Search, Filter, and Discover Improved model and endpoint search with case-insensitive matching. 📊 Better Insights at a Glance Enhanced Endpoint Metrics Get visibility into model performance with new metrics: Time to First Token (TTFT) Time Per Output Token (TPOT) Output Tokens per Second Kubernetes Monitoring Made Easy A unified view of your cluster, nodes, and usage—all in one place. Click-Through Model Links Quickly access Hugging Face or NIM model source pages right from your dashboard. 🧰 Support Gets Smarter Support Bundles On Demand Generate support bundles from your Kubernetes cluster to streamline troubleshooting with Nutanix Support. Minimum Requirements Kubernetes 1.31 , NVIDIA GPU Operator v25.3.0, NVIDIA Toolkit v1.17.5, and more. Supported GPUs: NVIDIA L40S, A100, H100, H100-NVL, and H200. For full software and GPU requirements, see the Nutanix Enterprise AI Guide . 🎯 Final Thought With this release, Nutanix Enterprise AI becomes even more robust—giving enterprises the tools they need to securely deploy and monitor GenAI workloads at scale, with greater control and visibility than ever before. Continue the conversation on the Nutanix Cloud Platform for AI forum .

latest_releases.title: Nutanix Kubernetes Platform 2.15.1
latest_releases.summary: NKP 2.15.1 is a maintenance release focused on stability, security, and smoother day-to-day operations. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. What’s New Bitnami Image Migration Resolved We’ve eliminated the dependency on Bitnami’s public catalog after their migration, ensuring images are consistently available without disruption. Fixes and Improvements Harbor UI Quota Display Storage provider quotas may still incorrectly appear as “Unlimited” in the Harbor UI, but configured limits remain enforced. Private Registry Deployments Applications deployed on the management cluster using the NCR private registry may fail due to certificate mismatches. A trusted CA configuration is recommended. Kommander Installation Reliability Certain persistent volume claims (PVCs) may prevent Kommander installation. Restarting the pod allows installation to continue. Rook Ceph on vSphere Some RHEL-based vSphere clusters may encounter errors when deploying Rook Ceph, impacting Velero and Loki object stores. Custom Cluster Banners Custom banners created on earlier versions are lost during upgrades and must be reapplied. UI Refresh Needed During cluster creation, UI options may dim until the page is refreshed. Limitations & Deprecations Air-gapped Trivy Scans Vulnerability scans require a manual database sync in air-gapped environments. Harbor on FIPS Harbor is not supported on FIPS clusters. Self-Signed Certificates By default, the NCR registry uses self-signed certificates. Workload clusters must be configured to trust these. OS & API Changes Ubuntu 20.04 support removed. RHEL 8.8 deprecated. apps.kommander.mesosphere.io/v1alpha2 API is deprecated in favor of v1alpha3 . The --charts-bundle flag is no longer required for Kommander installation.

latest_releases.title: Nutanix Kubernetes Platform 2.16
latest_releases.summary: Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP) 2.16 is here, bringing exciting new features, enhancements, and fixes to make your Kubernetes experience even better. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. Key Features and Enhancements Kubernetes 1.33 Support : NKP 2.16 now supports the latest Kubernetes version, 1.33, ensuring you're always up-to-date with the latest Kubernetes advancements. Rocky Linux 9.6 Support : Enjoy enhanced compatibility with Rocky Linux 9.6, expanding your operating system options. vGPU Node Pools : Optimize GPU resource utilization with support for vGPU-enabled node pools alongside passthrough GPUs in Nutanix infrastructure. Pre-flight Checks : The NKP CLI now includes pre-flight validation checks to detect common configuration and environment issues before cluster deployment or upgrade. Partner Catalog : Explore a wide range of partner applications through the new centralized partner catalog. License Upgrade : Easily upgrade your NKP licenses directly from the NKP user interface, streamlining your workflow. Resolved Issues Grafana Plugin Errors in Air-gapped Environments : We've fixed the issue where Grafana was attempting to download plugins in air-gapped clusters. Workload Cluster Deployment Issues : Resolved a memory leak in the cluster API addon provider helm (CAAPH) component that was causing newly created workload clusters to miss essential services. Scaling Issues : Fixed a problem where NKP clusters failed to scale down due to node pool replica configurations outside the current replica range. Security Updates Mitigated Security Vulnerabilities : NKP 2.16 includes important security updates, reinforcing our commitment to providing secure software. Upgrade to NKP 2.16 today and experience the latest enhancements and improvements. Have questions, continue the conversation in the NKP forums .

latest_releases.title: Nutanix Objects 5.2.1
latest_releases.summary: Nutanix Objects 5.2.1 is now available, bringing several key improvements and fixes to enhance your experience. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. Key Improvements and Fixes Resolved Race Condition : We've addressed a race condition (ENG-799005) that was impacting object store deployment and upgrade operations, ensuring smoother transitions. Bucket Size Calculation : An issue where bucket size didn't reduce to zero after object expiry when expiration and tiering were enabled has been fixed (ENG-800836). Known Issues and Considerations NKE and Prism Central Restoration : When Nutanix Kubernetes Engine (NKE) is enabled, restoring a Prism Central instance using Prism Central Backup and Restore (PCBR) may lead to inconsistencies in certain Insights Data Fabric (IDF) entity types (ENG-783153, ENG-786507). Nutanix Objects Browser on VPC with NAT : Launching the Nutanix Objects browser on a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) with Network Address Translation (NAT) configuration may encounter issues (ENG-758826). Upgrade Considerations To perform a dark site upgrade to Nutanix Objects version 5.1, ensure you download and extract the Microservices Platform (MSP) 2.6.0 bundle in the same web server location as the Nutanix Objects bundle. These release notes provide essential information for a successful upgrade and operation of Nutanix Objects 5.2.1. For detailed compatibility information, refer to the Software Interoperability Matrix on the Nutanix Support Portal. Have questions, continue the conversation in the Nutanix Objects forum .

latest_releases.title: Nutanix Move 6.0
latest_releases.summary: A Smarter, More Secure Move Nutanix Move 6.0 introduces thoughtful improvements that make migrations more reliable, more secure, and easier to monitor. It’s not just an update — it’s a reimagined experience for moving workloads with confidence. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. ✨ What’s New Upgrade Path Made Simple Direct in-place upgrade from Move 5.6.0. Versions 5.4.x and 5.5.x can still move forward through migration. Security Policy Migration Bring your security posture with you: seamlessly migrate VMware NSX policies into Nutanix Flow Network Security (FNS). Health at a Glance New View Metrics dashboard gives real-time insights into the appliance’s health, so you know exactly how Move is performing. Refined Experience Improved UI, tighter security controls, and a host of bug fixes deliver a smoother, more intuitive migration journey. ✅ Compatibility Updates AOS: 6.5 → 7.3.1 ESXi: 6.0 → 8.0 (with notes on TLS and licensing) Hyper-V: Windows Server 2012 → 2022 Files: 4.4.0 → 5.2.0 NSX: 3.2.3, 4.1.0 (for security policy migration) Prism Central: up to 2024.3.1 🛠️ Fixes You’ll Notice Smarter prechecks for network mapping to avoid surprises at cutover. Improved stability when working with scaled Prism Central . Better handling of guest OS IDs and disk order retention across platforms. Clearer error messages when Azure VM quotas run out. More reliable migrations when handling special characters in file server names. ⚠️ Known Issues (To Keep in Mind) Secure Boot VMs may require VirtIO 1.1.7 before cutover. Some NGT installations may downgrade VirtIO versions (fix in progress). Specific issues persist with vSAN 6.5 , Hyper-V differencing disks , and Azure Ultra SSDs as OS disks. A handful of migrations (e.g., AHV → AWS, Files migration states) require manual workarounds or retries. 📝 Notes Nutanix Move now reserves 172.17.0.0/16 and 172.18.0.0/16 for internal services. New permissions are required for ESXi source migrations, including Cryptographic Operations: Direct Access . Supported VirtIO version: 1.2.4 . The Bottom Line Nutanix Move 6.0 is all about making migrations safer, smarter, and more transparent . With security policy migration, real-time health metrics, and a host of refinements, it brings you closer to effortless workload mobility. Continue the conversation in the Nutanix Move forum .

latest_releases.title: Flow Network Security Next-Gen 5.0.1
latest_releases.summary: Flow Network Security Next-Gen version 5.0.1 is now available, bringing several key enhancements and improvements to your network security experience. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. What's New Cisco ACI Integration : Flow Network Security Next-Gen now integrates seamlessly with Cisco Application Centric Infrastructure (ACI), expanding your microsegmentation capabilities. Single-Stack Architecture : This release features a single-stack architecture, resulting in better resource utilization and higher performance compared to dual-stack configurations. Compatibility Requirements To ensure a smooth experience, make sure your environment meets the following compatibility requirements: AOS version 6.10 AHV version 20230302.100173 Prism Central version pc.2024.2.0.x Network Controller version 3.0.0 or later Known Issues While we've made significant improvements, we're aware of a couple of issues to watch out for: Default quarantine policies for VLAN policy scope may not be created if Flow Microsegmentation is enabled via API before Network Controller is enabled (NET-17450) Importing a large number of policies (especially those with 4000 service groups or more) may lead to an out-of-memory condition for the Flow service (NET-18440) Deployment Highlights This release supports various deployment scenarios, including VLAN only, VPC only, and mixed environments. For detailed instructions on installation and prerequisites, refer to the full release notes document. By addressing these key areas, Flow Network Security Next-Gen 5.0.1 aims to provide a more robust and efficient network security solution for your organization.

latest_releases.title: Nutanix Database Service 2.9
latest_releases.summary: Nutanix Database Service (NDB) 2.9 brings fresh power, resilience, and simplicity to database lifecycle management—whether you’re running Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or MySQL. This release delivers major innovations in disaster recovery, high availability, security, and user experience, so your databases stay protected, performant, and effortless to manage. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. ✨ What’s New Oracle Disaster Recovery Full integration with Oracle Data Guard —setup and manage DR directly from the NDB console, API, or CLI. SQL Server at Scale Support for multi-database groups : up to 5 groups per VM, each with 35 databases (175 per server). Secure communication with WinRM over HTTPS , meeting enterprise-grade security requirements. Enterprise Security Built-In SELinux enforcing mode now supported for MongoDB, Oracle, and PostgreSQL servers. Protection against human error, ransomware, and corruption with NDB Control Plane Backup & Recovery . High Availability for MySQL Provision HA MySQL instances across Nutanix clusters for fault-tolerant deployments. Cloud-Init Support Standardized Linux VM configuration at runtime for faster, more reliable provisioning. Smarter Storage Insights New storage consumption reporting gives deep visibility into usage by databases, clones, and Time Machines. Accessibility Matters Major improvements aligned with WCAG 2.2 Level AA for a more inclusive experience. Bulk Patching at Scale Manage up to 80 DB server VMs per maintenance window for faster patch cycles. ✅ Resolved Issues SQL Server upgrades and patching are now more reliable, with fixes for cluster instance reinstalls, in-place restores, and LDAP prechecks. PostgreSQL stability improvements for HA deployments and rollback handling. Oracle RAC standby creation and replication errors resolved. MongoDB restores from snapshots and PITR are now seamless. UI fixes, including VLAN selection accuracy. Control plane upgraded from unsupported PostgreSQL version 10.23 to remove vulnerabilities. ⚠️ Known Issues Upgrade quirks : High-frequency backup environments may see temporary Time Machine alerts during upgrades. Storage efficiency : Periodic fstrim must be manually enabled on Linux VMs to prevent bloated volumes. Oracle : RAC/PDB clone refresh issues and restrictions with SUSE + XFS remain. SQL Server : Certain FCI installs may fail with Analysis Services present; VirtIO 1.2.4 is not supported. PostgreSQL : Key handling errors on RHEL 9.4; use updated OOB profiles. MongoDB : Aborted sharded cluster provisions may require manual cleanup. UI : Some dashboard tiles may not reflect Object Storage usage accurately. 🔗 Compatibility Highlights Platforms : AOS 7.3, 7.0, 6.10, 6.5; vSphere 7.0 & 8.0; AHV supported via AOS. Databases : Oracle 11.2 → 21c (with ASM/HA limitations) SQL Server 2014 → 2022 (AG/FCI support varies by edition) PostgreSQL 13 → 17 (Community + EDB) MongoDB 6.0 → 8.0 (Community + Enterprise) MySQL 8

This release brings expanded Kubernetes compatibility, deeper automation, stronger security foundations, and powerful new infrastructure features designed to scale the modern hybrid cloud. Build security rules independently with a new rule-centric policy model for more precise traffic control. Secure workloads using domain names. Define policies with fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) instead of manually managing changing IP addresses. Organize security by project. Manage policies, groups, and security resources within project boundaries for stronger tenant isolation and simpler administration. Monitor policy usage with built-in analytics. Use new Flows and Rules dashboards to understand how security policies are performing across your environment. Improvements Simplify Kubernetes onboarding. Reduce setup steps and automate cluster registration to get protected faster. Automatically detect Kubernetes networking. Discover service IPs, ports, load balancers, and egress gateways without manual policy updates. Increase service resilience. Improve availability with active-active service insertion and stronger disaster recovery support. Scale larger environments. Support significantly more security rules and address groups for growing deployments. Improve accessibility. Enhance keyboard navigation and assistive technology support, including better focus controls and inactivity warnings. Install automatically with AOS 7.6 and Prism Central pc.7.6. Deploy or upgrade with Flow Network Security Next-Gen included as part of the bundled software package. Fixes Improve failover reliability. Resolve an issue affecting planned failovers for protected virtual machines. Fix Flow enablement on dual-stack deployments. Restore successful enablement through both the UI and API. Strengthen role-based access controls. Prevent users from viewing security policies outside their assigned scope. Reduce unnecessary memory growth. Fix an issue that increased Prism Central memory usage after recovery operations.

latest_releases.title: Nutanix Guest Tools (NGT) 4.6
latest_releases.summary: NGT 4.6 makes guest VM management simpler and more reliable. New Configure Nutanix Guest Tools on supported virtual machines without mounting a CD-ROM, making setup faster and reducing operational steps. Restore individual files directly to AHV virtual machines using Nutanix v4 APIs, simplifying file recovery without restoring an entire VM. Improvements Renew NGT server certificates automatically before they expire to reduce maintenance and avoid unexpected disruptions. Improve installation reliability across a wider range of Linux distributions. Strengthen security by updating bundled Python and OpenSSL components to address multiple vulnerabilities. Improve Remote Procedure Call (RPC) reliability for guest-to-host communication. Eliminate unnecessary warning messages after upgrading NGT on Linux virtual machines. Prevent false CD-ROM mount errors on systems that do not have an available CD-ROM slot, resulting in a cleaner and more accurate management experience. Compatibility Bundle NGT 4.6 with AOS 7.6 . Continue to offer NGT 4.6 as both a standalone download and as part of the AOS 7.6 release. Known Issue Windows Server 2008 R2 is no longer supported for NGT 4.2 and later. Upgrade to a newer version of Windows to install NGT 4.6 successfully.

latest_releases.title: Nutanix Database Service 2.11
latest_releases.summary: Nutanix Database Service 2.11 makes managing enterprise databases more flexible, resilient, and secure. This release adds new disaster recovery capabilities, simplifies scaling for high-availability deployments, strengthens security, and streamlines day-to-day database operations. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. New Scale SQL Server and PostgreSQL high-availability clusters by adding or removing database nodes without reprovisioning or downtime. Protect MySQL high-availability deployments with automated snapshots, log backups, point-in-time recovery, and in-place restores. Encrypt MySQL and EDB PostgreSQL databases using externally managed encryption keys to better protect data at rest. Enable disaster recovery for PostgreSQL high-availability databases with built-in replication and failover across sites. Store PostgreSQL write-ahead logs in Nutanix Objects for more scalable and resilient recovery. Share databases and clones with granular access levels so teams can safely collaborate without requiring administrator privileges. Centralize audit logs for user actions across the UI, CLI, and APIs for improved governance and compliance. Expand MongoDB sharded clusters online by adding shards or routing nodes without downtime. Generate more targeted diagnostic bundles by selecting specific log categories and time ranges. Choose Oracle Data Guard IP addresses directly from the web console during disaster recovery configuration. Run built-in upgrade readiness checks before upgrading to identify and resolve issues early. Configure custom PostgreSQL collation settings during provisioning and cloning to support application-specific requirements. Improvements Restore and clone encrypted MongoDB databases more seamlessly while automatically updating encryption keys. Provision new SQL Server databases with Volume Groups by default for a more modern storage experience. Speed SQL Server provisioning from backups while improving storage layout and post-provisioning performance. Increase SQL Server Storage Spaces scalability with support for larger volumes and faster restore operations. View Time Machine snapshots in a sortable list for improved accessibility and easier navigation. Strengthen security by routing Prism API communication through NDB, eliminating the need to store Prism credentials on database servers. Resume backup operations sooner during control plane upgrades to reduce recovery point exposure. Simplify Windows database server provisioning by removing the dependency on Agent VMs. Upgrade the NDB control plane to Rocky Linux 9.8 for improved security, stability, and performance. Add support for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.10 on MySQL, MariaDB, and PostgreSQL deployments. Upgrade to Python 3.11 and Ansible 2.18 for better performance, security, and platform compatibility. Migrate virtual machines directly to Projects 2.0 . Migrate security policies to Projects 2.0 alongside your workloads. Move VMs from ESXi to AHV using zero-copy migration with supported external storage. Migrate data with support for Federated Files Server . Migrate workloads from ESXi and AHV to Nutanix Government Cloud Clusters (GC2) on AWS GovCloud . Preserve UEFI and Secure Boot settings when migrating supported VMs between AHV and AWS. Use additional external storage arrays, including Dell PowerStore and Pure Storage FlashArray (Everpure) . Manage migrations with support for Prism Central 7.6 . Integrate with CyberArk (technical preview) for credential management. Migrate a broader range of Windows and Linux operating systems across AHV, AWS, and Azure. Improvements Keep IPv6 settings intact during Windows migrations, including systems running non-English operating systems. Complete migration plans even if an individual VM encounters an issue during cutover. Sign in reliably with Prism Central IAM group accounts after upgrading Move. Configure and edit bandwidth policies without interface errors. Improve migration reliability during VMware tag retrieval and cutover operations. Remove VMware Tools more cleanly during Windows VM migrations. Prevent target VMs from powering on when a source migration has failed. Improve IP address retention for VLAN-based networks without IP pools. Increase migration reliability for Linux VMs using non-root accounts with sudo privileges. Speed up inventory collection for large Hyper-V environments. Improve disk mapping accuracy during AWS migrations. Provide clearer guidance when AWS permissions are required to preserve Secure Boot settings. Fixes Fixed Windows VM authentication timing issues during AHV-to-AHV migrations. latest_releases.title: Nutanix Objects 5.4

New Improve performance by removing load balancer VMs from supported AHV deployments, reducing infrastructure complexity while enabling unmanaged network deployments with manual network configuration. Reduce upgrade downtime with rolling upgrades that keep I/O disruption shorter during Nutanix Objects Service upgrades. Simplify MSP image management by automatically using the appropriate Microservices Platform (MSP) platform bundle for supported Prism Central and Objects versions. Protect data with more precise access controls by creating object-level bucket policies based on object name prefixes or tags directly from Prism Central, the CLI, or APIs. Automate more workflows with new v4 APIs for buckets, data movement targets, and storage backends. Improvements Deploy more flexibly by supporting unmanaged networks for AHV deployments without requiring an AHV-managed network. Modernize deployments and upgrades with improved compatibility between Nutanix Objects, Prism Central, and the MSP platform. latest_releases.title: Nutanix Files 5.4

Improvements Lock down server access : Control administrative access to file server VMs by restricting command-line operations or turning off SSH entirely. Automate disaster recovery upgrades : Experience seamless failover protection with legacy clusters automatically adopting modern asymmetrical disaster recovery upon updating. Strengthen time synchronization : Safeguard clock accuracy across your servers with secure, authenticated NTP configuration options. Fixes Eliminate false capacity limits : Resolved an issue causing premature out-of-space warnings on SMB shares with available storage space. Prevent performance slowdowns : Fixed high latency and memory alignment issues during heavy file creation and auditing workflows. Ensure uninterrupted failovers : Fixed an issue where domain service principal names were skipped during disaster recovery failover tasks. Maintain continuous replication : Resolved issues causing NearSync and snapshot replications to stall or fail during site address modifications or high snapshot volumes. Restore non-admin share management : Allowed delegated Power Users to view and manage open files using standard administrative tools. Have questions? latest_releases.summary: Nutanix Objects 5.3.1.1 delivers important security updates to help keep object storage environments protected and up to date. Updates the MSP cluster automatically as part of the Nutanix Objects upgrade, ensuring the required security fixes are applied. Before You Upgrade Upgrade to the latest MSP version before deploying or upgrading a Nutanix Objects cluster. Use the MSP Platform bundle for dark-site deployments and upgrades running Prism Central 7.5 with Objects 5.3. Known Issues This release includes several known issues affecting specific configurations and workflows. Key considerations include: Configure erasure coding manually when deploying Objects 5.3.x on AOS 7.6 clusters using a 1N:2D configuration to avoid suboptimal performance. Recreate legacy destination buckets before configuring replication from buckets that use the newer multipart delimiters. Use the corresponding floating IP address if the Objects Browser does not load correctly for an object store deployed on a VPC with NAT. Review certificate requirements before upgrading from a version earlier than 5.0. Certificate chains containing keys smaller than 2048 bits can prevent the upgrade from completing. For the complete list of known issues, workarounds, and supported versions, refer to the Nutanix Objects 5.3.1.1 Release Notes and the Software Interoperability Matrix in the Nutanix Support Portal. latest_releases.title: Nutanix Move 6.3.3
latest_releases.summary: Nutanix Move 6.3.3 introduces DirectPath, a new migration method that transfers virtual machine (VM) disk data directly from VMware ESXi to Nutanix AHV without requiring the VMware Virtual Disk Development Kit (VDDK). The release also includes security updates, UI improvements, and bug fixes. For administrators planning a migration, the most important consideration is deployment compatibility: Move 6.3.3 supports new deployments only. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. Action required: New deployments only Nutanix Move 6.3.3 cannot be installed through an upgrade from an earlier release. Upgrading from 6.3.3 to another version is also unsupported. Before deploying, administrators should review the supported platform versions, required VMware permissions, and known migration limitations. VM migrations using ESXi as the source require two permissions: Provisioning: Allow virtual machine download Cryptographic Operations: Direct Access Administrators should ensure the necessary permissions are configured before starting migrations. What's new and improved DirectPath: VM migration without VDDK DirectPath introduces a new approach to transferring VM disk data from VMware ESXi to Nutanix AHV. Instead of requiring VDDK, DirectPath transfers disk data directly between the source and destination platforms. This removes the VDDK dependency from the migration method. For infrastructure teams, DirectPath provides an additional option when planning ESXi-to-AHV migrations. Security, UI, and bug fixes Move 6.3.3 includes security improvements, user interface enhancements, and resolved issues. The release notes do not provide individual details for these changes. Availability and compatibility Move 6.3.3 supports the following platform versions: Platform Supported versions Nutanix AOS 6.10, 7.0, 7.3, 7.5, 7.6 Prism Central pc.2024.3, pc.7.3, pc.7.5, pc.7.6 VMware ESXi 6.5, 6.7, 7.0 (including Updates 1–3), 8.0 (including Updates 1 and 3) VMware vCenter 6.7, 7.0 (including Updates 1–3), 8.0, 8.0 Update 3, 9.0 ESXi hosts using a free license are not supported. The supported Nutanix VirtIO version is 1.2.5 . Known issues and migration considerations Several known issues may affect migration planning and cutover operations. DirectPath datastore naming conflicts. Migrations can fail when two clusters in the same datacenter contain datastores with identical names but different contents. To resolve this issue, assign unique datastore names and mount the datastore to another host as required. Cutover failures. If a cutover fails because target VM properties exceed available cluster resources, resizing the VM alone may not resolve the issue. Delete the previously created target VM from Prism Element or Prism Central before retrying the cutover. Secure Boot compatibility. latest_releases.title: Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP) 2.19
latest_releases.summary: Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP) 2.19 expands Kubernetes deployment and management with bare-metal support, simplified cluster upgrades, and new capabilities for AI workloads. The release also adds Kubernetes 1.36 support, AHV virtual machine management, and improvements to AI Navigator. Administrators upgrading existing environments should review changes to Prism Central projects, container registry authentication, and deprecated components before proceeding. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. Action Required: Prepare for NKP 2.19 Several changes require attention before installation or upgrade. Prism Central Projects 2.0: Clusters must use a single Prism Central project across control plane and worker nodes. Before upgrading NKP 2.18 clusters spanning multiple projects, consolidate all nodes into one project. DockerHub authentication: Management clusters without an existing Nutanix DockerHub registry token must provide one during upgrade. Catalog migration: GitRepository-based catalogs are no longer supported. Migrate remaining AppDeployment resources to OCIRepository-based catalogs. Removed CLI flag: The --kommander-applications-repository flag is no longer supported for nkp install kommander or nkp upgrade kommander . Kubernetes Dashboard: NKP replaces Kubernetes Dashboard with Headlamp. Existing Dashboard instances remain running after upgrade, but Nutanix recommends migrating to Headlamp as soon as possible. The nkp upgrade workspace command is also deprecated. Use the supported cluster or platform application upgrade workflows instead. What's New and Improved Deploy Kubernetes Directly on Bare Metal NKP 2.19 introduces NKP Metal , enabling Kubernetes deployment and management on physical servers. Using Foundation Central and the NKP host inventory, administrators can image and register hosts, assign them to workspaces, and create bare-metal clusters. Physical worker node pools can also be added to VM-based clusters. This provides direct access to compute, networking, storage, and accelerators for AI, GPU computing, and edge workloads. Simplified Cluster Upgrades ClusterClass workload clusters, including Nutanix and EKS clusters, now support per-cluster upgrades through the NKP UI or a single CLI command. The workflow upgrades platform applications before Kubernetes, cluster infrastructure, and related add-ons. For non-ClusterClass clusters, the new nkp upgrade platform-apps command upgrades platform applications independently. The management cluster must first be upgraded to NKP 2.19. Manage Virtual Machines Alongside Containers NKP 2.19 introduces AHV virtual machine management through VM Operator. Platform teams can provision, update, monitor, and manage Linux and Windows VMs using Kubernetes APIs and declarative workflows. items.title: CVE-2026-100223 Windows NTFS Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
items.summary:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists when reparse points are created by sandboxed processes allowing sandbox escape. An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could use the sandbox escape to elevate privileges on an affected system. 

To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker would first have to log on to the system, and then run a specially crafted application to take control over the affected system.

The security update addresses the vulnerability by preventing sandboxed processes from creating reparse points targeting inaccessible files.

The security update addresses the vulnerability by correcting the way that WER handles and executes files.

items.title: AOS 7.3.0.1
items.summary: AOS 7.3.0.1 is here — a refinement release that polishes your experience with improved stability, sharper compatibility, and critical bug fixes. It’s everything you love about AOS, made even smoother. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. 🌟 What’s New One Small Fix. One Giant Leap for Stability. Resolved a rare but critical issue that caused Stargate and Curator services to fail on deduplication-enabled clusters after upgrading to AOS 7.3. ⚙️ Bundled Software AOS 7.3.0.1 ships with: NCC 5.2.0 NGT 4.3 Foundation 5.9 LCM 3.2 Flow Network Security 4.2.1 🛠️ Resolved Issues — Fast. Reliable. Resilient. 🔧 Stargate stability restored. Previously, enabling deduplication could crash key services — now resolved. 🚧 Known Issues — Heads-Up So You’re a Step Ahead AHV Management Post-upgrade, cluster CPU features may downgrade NIC deployment errors using v4 API Flash mode toggle may fail with volume groups Data Replication & Protection Force delete tasks may hang Snapshot replication quirks with NearSync Manual VM recovery may omit NIC Prism & NGT Web console may fail under high load NGT service may fail post-upgrade Infrastructure & Services On-disk deduplication may auto-disable on large fresh deployments VM memory changes round up on AHV Networking Virtual switch updates may fail if launched from Prism Central 📦 Upgrade Essentials Use Life Cycle Manager (LCM) via Prism to upgrade. V3 VM APIs are not supported in Prism Element. Stick with Prism Central. Host-based reservation is deprecated —switch to segment-based. VLAN Discovery is disabled by default for safety. Compatibility with NetBackup 8.2 requires an EEB from Veritas. ✅ Feature Support by Hypervisor Whether you're running AHV, ESXi, or Hyper-V, AOS 7.3.0.1 brings robust support across critical features like: Self-service restore Async DR with NearSync VM roles and RBAC vGPU, vNUMA, and whole-node maintenance mode (For full compatibility, check the matrix in the Support Portal ).

items.title: Nutanix Enterprise AI 2.4
items.summary: A powerful step forward in performance, control, and simplicity. Nutanix Enterprise AI 2.4 introduces meaningful improvements that make managing inference endpoints faster, smarter, and more flexible—across edge, on-prem, or cloud environments. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. 🧠 Smarter Performance, Built-In CPU and GPU Acceleration Choose between GPU or Intel® AMX-enabled CPU acceleration for optimal performance—tailored to your workload. Expanded Model Support Pre-validated support for new Hugging Face and NVIDIA models including Llama 3 , Mistral , Stable Diffusion , and more. Now with NVIDIA H200 GPU support Tap into the next generation of high-performance AI acceleration. 🛠️ A Simpler, Smoother Workflow New Endpoint Creation Wizard A guided, intuitive flow for building endpoints—no YAML needed. Create Endpoints from Imported Models Go from model import to deployment in a single click. Auto Model Size Detection Model size is now automatically detected when importing from Hugging Face. HTTP Proxy Support Easily connect to external services—even from air-gapped or dark sites. 🔐 More Control, More Confidence Fine-Grained Access to Models Control exactly which models your users can import or upload—via catalog, direct URLs, or manual upload. Search, Filter, and Discover Improved model and endpoint search with case-insensitive matching. 📊 Better Insights at a Glance Enhanced Endpoint Metrics Get visibility into model performance with new metrics: Time to First Token (TTFT) Time Per Output Token (TPOT) Output Tokens per Second Kubernetes Monitoring Made Easy A unified view of your cluster, nodes, and usage—all in one place. Click-Through Model Links Quickly access Hugging Face or NIM model source pages right from your dashboard. 🧰 Support Gets Smarter Support Bundles On Demand Generate support bundles from your Kubernetes cluster to streamline troubleshooting with Nutanix Support. Minimum Requirements Kubernetes 1.31 , NVIDIA GPU Operator v25.3.0, NVIDIA Toolkit v1.17.5, and more. Supported GPUs: NVIDIA L40S, A100, H100, H100-NVL, and H200. For full software and GPU requirements, see the Nutanix Enterprise AI Guide . 🎯 Final Thought With this release, Nutanix Enterprise AI becomes even more robust—giving enterprises the tools they need to securely deploy and monitor GenAI workloads at scale, with greater control and visibility than ever before. Continue the conversation on the Nutanix Cloud Platform for AI forum .

items.title: Nutanix Kubernetes Platform 2.15.1
items.summary: NKP 2.15.1 is a maintenance release focused on stability, security, and smoother day-to-day operations. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. What’s New Bitnami Image Migration Resolved We’ve eliminated the dependency on Bitnami’s public catalog after their migration, ensuring images are consistently available without disruption. Fixes and Improvements Harbor UI Quota Display Storage provider quotas may still incorrectly appear as “Unlimited” in the Harbor UI, but configured limits remain enforced. Private Registry Deployments Applications deployed on the management cluster using the NCR private registry may fail due to certificate mismatches. A trusted CA configuration is recommended. Kommander Installation Reliability Certain persistent volume claims (PVCs) may prevent Kommander installation. Restarting the pod allows installation to continue. Rook Ceph on vSphere Some RHEL-based vSphere clusters may encounter errors when deploying Rook Ceph, impacting Velero and Loki object stores. Custom Cluster Banners Custom banners created on earlier versions are lost during upgrades and must be reapplied. UI Refresh Needed During cluster creation, UI options may dim until the page is refreshed. Limitations & Deprecations Air-gapped Trivy Scans Vulnerability scans require a manual database sync in air-gapped environments. Harbor on FIPS Harbor is not supported on FIPS clusters. Self-Signed Certificates By default, the NCR registry uses self-signed certificates. Workload clusters must be configured to trust these. OS & API Changes Ubuntu 20.04 support removed. RHEL 8.8 deprecated. apps.kommander.mesosphere.io/v1alpha2 API is deprecated in favor of v1alpha3 . The --charts-bundle flag is no longer required for Kommander installation.

items.title: Nutanix Objects 5.2.1

items.title: Nutanix Move 6.0
items.summary: A Smarter, More Secure Move Nutanix Move 6.0 introduces thoughtful improvements that make migrations more reliable, more secure, and easier to monitor. Refined Experience Improved UI, tighter security controls, and a host of bug fixes deliver a smoother, more intuitive migration journey. ✅ Compatibility Updates AOS: 6.5 → 7.3.1 ESXi: 6.0 → 8.0 (with notes on TLS and licensing) Hyper-V: Windows Server 2012 → 2022 Files: 4.4.0 → 5.2.0 NSX: 3.2.3, 4.1.0 (for security policy migration) Prism Central: up to 2024.3.1 🛠️ Fixes You’ll Notice Smarter prechecks for network mapping to avoid surprises at cutover. Improved stability when working with scaled Prism Central . Better handling of guest OS IDs and disk order retention across platforms. Clearer error messages when Azure VM quotas run out. More reliable migrations when handling special characters in file server names. ⚠️ Known Issues (To Keep in Mind) Secure Boot VMs may require VirtIO 1.1.7 before cutover. The Bottom Line Nutanix Move 6.0 is all about making migrations safer, smarter, and more transparent . With security policy migration, real-time health metrics, and a host of refinements, it brings you closer to effortless workload mobility. Continue the conversation in the Nutanix Move forum .

Streamline cluster connectivity using Nutanix Konnector 1.0.0 for hybrid and air-gapped environment management. Fixes Prevent snapshot corruption during unexpected system crashes by ensuring snapshot secret fragments complete cleanly before saving. Restore default namespaces reliably without conflicts from pre-existing system resources. Want to dig deeper, share what you’re seeing, or swap ideas with other users? items.title: Nutanix Database Service 2.10.1.4
items.summary: This release introduces expanded platform capabilities, broadened database version support, and targeted stability enhancements designed to keep your database management seamless and reliable. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. New Expand platform compatibility with updated OS support across modern Linux distributions, including RHEL 9.7, OEL 9.7, Rocky Linux 9.7, Ubuntu 24.04, and Debian 12. Scale enterprise workloads with expanded engine version support across Oracle, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, MySQL, and MariaDB deployments. Enhance storage flexibility with initial support for oracleasmlib v3 drivers on supported Oracle setups. Improvements Strengthen system security with critical control plane security fixes. Improve operational reliability across High Availability (HA) clusters during post-recovery operations. Optimize storage health with improved guidance for automated storage trimming on Linux database VMs. Fixes Resolve SSL errors caused by missing Java keystore imports during post-recovery CA certificate syncs. Clean up temporary files automatically post-upgrade on databases running non-SLA profiles. Prevent false critical alerts on high-frequency backup time machines during active system upgrades. Want to dig deeper, share what you’re seeing, or swap ideas with other users? Keep the conversation going in the Nutanix Database Service forum , your next great solution might be one reply away.

items.title: NCM Self-Service 4.4
items.summary: NCM Self-Service VM 4.4 brings Self-Service compatibility forward while providing supported upgrade paths from previous releases. This release does not introduce new features or fixes specific to Self-Service VM. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. Improvements Upgrade to Self-Service VM 4.4 from versions 4.0 through 4.3.1 using the supported upgrade paths. Versions 4.0 and 4.1 must first upgrade to version 4.3 before moving to 4.4. Use Self-Service 4.4 features and improvements with Self-Service VM 4.4. No new capabilities are specific to the Self-Service VM functionality in this release. Continue using supported browsers , including Microsoft Edge 12+, Mozilla Firefox 22+, Google Chrome 45+, and Apple Safari 10+. Known Issues Express Launch: Projects may not appear in the Project selection menu, resulting in a “No valid project found” message. Contact Nutanix Support for assistance. Large scale-out environments: Deployments reaching 47,000 single-VM applications may run out of disk space in the MSP partition. Secure Boot: Self-Service VM may not start when UEFI and Secure Boot are enabled. Restored environments: Some projects may encounter issues with variable creation, project updates, or project assignment after restoring a backup. Active Directory users: After restoring a backup to a new Self-Service VM, the Projects page may not display all previously added Active Directory users, although they remain visible when editing users and groups. Upgrade note: The LCM framework for Self-Service VM does not support upgrades, including Calm, Epsilon, and Policy services. Follow the documented Self-Service VM upgrade path when moving to version 4.4. Want to dig deeper, share what you’re seeing, or swap ideas with other users? Share individual models securely. Give specific users or groups access to selected imported models without exposing your entire model catalog. License Agent Gateway capabilities separately. Use trusted documents to generate more relevant answers with citations that link back to the source content. Use fine-tuning with general availability. Import model files from NFS or S3-compatible storage and deploy them without requiring access to external registries. Import additional NVIDIA NIMs. Deploy supported NIMs beyond the pre-validated catalog using container images hosted in the NVIDIA NGC registry. Use MCP with general availability. Manage MCP client keys more easily and forward required request headers to MCP servers. Scale local endpoints across multiple GPU nodes. A new tech preview lets supported models use multiple GPU nodes with the vLLM inference engine. Offload KV cache to CPU memory. A new tech preview gives local endpoints another way to manage GPU resources by moving KV cache storage to CPU memory. Deploy more pre-validated models. Add support for new Mistral and NVIDIA Nemotron models, including Mistral Large 3 and NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra. Improvements View and download MCP server logs from the console. Monitor server activity and retrieve logs for troubleshooting and analysis without leaving Nutanix Enterprise AI. Use Anthropic Messages API with unified endpoints. Agent Gateway unified endpoints now support the Messages API specification for Anthropic provider APIs. Set more precise rate limits. items.title: Nutanix Move 6.3.3
items.summary: Nutanix Move 6.3.3 introduces DirectPath, a new migration method that transfers virtual machine (VM) disk data directly from VMware ESXi to Nutanix AHV without requiring the VMware Virtual Disk Development Kit (VDDK). The release also includes security updates, UI improvements, and bug fixes. For administrators planning a migration, the most important consideration is deployment compatibility: Move 6.3.3 supports new deployments only. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. Action required: New deployments only Nutanix Move 6.3.3 cannot be installed through an upgrade from an earlier release. Upgrading from 6.3.3 to another version is also unsupported. Before deploying, administrators should review the supported platform versions, required VMware permissions, and known migration limitations. VM migrations using ESXi as the source require two permissions: Provisioning: Allow virtual machine download Cryptographic Operations: Direct Access Administrators should ensure the necessary permissions are configured before starting migrations. What's new and improved DirectPath: VM migration without VDDK DirectPath introduces a new approach to transferring VM disk data from VMware ESXi to Nutanix AHV. Instead of requiring VDDK, DirectPath transfers disk data directly between the source and destination platforms. This removes the VDDK dependency from the migration method. For infrastructure teams, DirectPath provides an additional option when planning ESXi-to-AHV migrations. Security, UI, and bug fixes Move 6.3.3 includes security improvements, user interface enhancements, and resolved issues. The release notes do not provide individual details for these changes. Availability and compatibility Move 6.3.3 supports the following platform versions: Platform Supported versions Nutanix AOS 6.10, 7.0, 7.3, 7.5, 7.6 Prism Central pc.2024.3, pc.7.3, pc.7.5, pc.7.6 VMware ESXi 6.5, 6.7, 7.0 (including Updates 1–3), 8.0 (including Updates 1 and 3) VMware vCenter 6.7, 7.0 (including Updates 1–3), 8.0, 8.0 Update 3, 9.0 ESXi hosts using a free license are not supported. The supported Nutanix VirtIO version is 1.2.5 . Known issues and migration considerations Several known issues may affect migration planning and cutover operations. DirectPath datastore naming conflicts. Migrations can fail when two clusters in the same datacenter contain datastores with identical names but different contents. To resolve this issue, assign unique datastore names and mount the datastore to another host as required. Cutover failures. If a cutover fails because target VM properties exceed available cluster resources, resizing the VM alone may not resolve the issue. Delete the previously created target VM from Prism Element or Prism Central before retrying the cutover. Secure Boot compatibility. CentOS 8.4 and 8.5 VMs configured with Secure Boot may fail to boot on AHV after migration. The documented workarounds are to disable Secure Boot or reset its keys th

items.title: Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP) 2.19
items.summary: Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP) 2.19 expands Kubernetes deployment and management with bare-metal support, simplified cluster upgrades, and new capabilities for AI workloads. The release also adds Kubernetes 1.36 support, AHV virtual machine management, and improvements to AI Navigator. Administrators upgrading existing environments should review changes to Prism Central projects, container registry authentication, and deprecated components before proceeding. Review the detailed release notes before deploying any product updates. Action Required: Prepare for NKP 2.19 Several changes require attention before installation or upgrade. Prism Central Projects 2.0: Clusters must use a single Prism Central project across control plane and worker nodes. Before upgrading NKP 2.18 clusters spanning multiple projects, consolidate all nodes into one project. DockerHub authentication: Management clusters without an existing Nutanix DockerHub registry token must provide one during upgrade. Catalog migration: GitRepository-based catalogs are no longer supported. Migrate remaining AppDeployment resources to OCIRepository-based catalogs. Removed CLI flag: The --kommander-applications-repository flag is no longer supported for nkp install kommander or nkp upgrade kommander . Kubernetes Dashboard: NKP replaces Kubernetes Dashboard with Headlamp. Existing Dashboard instances remain running after upgrade, but Nutanix recommends migrating to Headlamp as soon as possible. The nkp upgrade workspace command is also deprecated. Use the supported cluster or platform application upgrade workflows instead. What's New and Improved Deploy Kubernetes Directly on Bare Metal NKP 2.19 introduces NKP Metal , enabling Kubernetes deployment and management on physical servers. Using Foundation Central and the NKP host inventory, administrators can image and register hosts, assign them to workspaces, and create bare-metal clusters. Physical worker node pools can also be added to VM-based clusters. This provides direct access to compute, networking, storage, and accelerators for AI, GPU computing, and edge workloads. Simplified Cluster Upgrades ClusterClass workload clusters, including Nutanix and EKS clusters, now support per-cluster upgrades through the NKP UI or a single CLI command. The workflow upgrades platform applications before Kubernetes, cluster infrastructure, and related add-ons. For non-ClusterClass clusters, the new nkp upgrade platform-apps command upgrades platform applications independently. The management cluster must first be upgraded to NKP 2.19. Manage Virtual Machines Alongside Containers NKP 2.19 introduces AHV virtual machine management through VM Operator. Platform teams can provision, update, monitor, and manage Linux and Windows VMs using Kubernetes APIs and declarative workflows. items.title: Increased Azure tag limit for Nutanix resources:
items.summary: Increased the Azure tag limit from 15 to 50 for Nutanix resources.

items.title: AVD:
items.summary: "Desktop Admin" RBAC Role Error: Resolved an issue in Nutanix-enabled environments where administrators with the "Desktop Admin" RBAC role may not have been able to create or update desktop images. Failed Desktop image task when boot diagnostics is enabled: Resolved an issue where, if boot diagnostics was enabled, updating a desktop image may have failed.

items.title: NME Install Terraform Module is Now Public Preview:
items.summary: Download the latest module at https://github.com/Get-Nerdio/NME-Terraform . Additional Terraform modules for NME management capabilities will be added in future releases.

items.title: Console Connect:
items.summary: UK Region Support: Expanded regional availability to include the UK Region. Updated Favicon: Console Connect favicon now reflects the new Nerdio logo.

items.title: ControlUp
items.summary: Integration is Now End of Maintenance (EOM): Nerdio's integration with ControlUp will no longer be developed moving forward. Starting with this release, the ControlUp integration settings have been removed for new installations of Nerdio Manager and for any existing deployments where the integration is not configured. Existing deployments where the integration is configured are unaffected, and Nerdio will continue to support the integration, including critical bugfixes.

items.title: AVD Hybrid on Nutanix: Desktop image management support is now available!
Device & App Management:
items.summary: Intune & Windows 365: Error when editing Windows 365 items in US Government tenants: Resolved an issue where the error Could not find a property named 'userExperienceType' may be displayed. The user experience type function is not supported by government tenants. This error has been suppressed. Intune User Experience call optimizations: The app service option IntuneUxHistory:Enabled may be added with a value of false to fully disable the user experience history data if desired. Unified App Management: Error when deploying Winget applications which contain unexpected version characters: Resolved an issue where the error No newer package versions are available from the configured sources may be returned during deployment if the application version contains the characters < or >. In this scenario, the source and target version are now treated as identical and no action is taken.

items.title: New Menu & All Features Page:
items.summary: Introduced a cleaner, more intuitive three-tier navigational menu. While off by default, users can enable it via the New Menu toggle in the top-left corner. A new All Features page provides a centralized, searchable view of every feature available within Nerdio Manager, and is only accessible when the new menu is enabled.

items.title: Localization Support:
items.summary: Nerdio Manager is now localized for Japanese. Users can select their desired supported language by clicking on their display name in the upper-right corner. Support for additional languages is coming soon!

items.title: Intune Policy Studio (Public Preview):
items.summary: Introduced a new Policy Studio feature that takes Nerdio Manager's Intune policy management capabilities to the next level with two key capabilities: Settings Explorer surfaces Intune policies alongside their settings and assigned values, with real-time search across policy names, settings, and values. Policy Results shows in-scope policies for a selected device or group, with conflict and duplication flags surfaced inline. Note Device configuration policies are supported with this initial release, however some settings may be unavailable. Support for additional Intune policy types is planned.

items.title: Intune Script Management:
items.summary: The same editing, versioning, back-up, and recovery capabilities that Nerdio Manager offers for Intune policies are now available for Intune platform scripts!

items.title: AVD Hybrid Support on Nutanix AHV is now Public Preview!
items.summary: New features included in this release: Re-image and re-size of session hosts App Attach support Unified Application Management (UAM) support Scripted Actions support Session Time Limits support Custom Views support Please see our AVD Hybrid KB for more details.

items.title: End of Support for AVD Classic.
items.summary: Nerdio Manager for Enterprise 8.0 will be the last version that supports AVD Classic tenants and host pools. Microsoft will retire AVD Classic on September 30, 2026. After this date, regardless of which version of Nerdio Manager is deployed, AVD Classic will no longer function. Customers still using AVD Classic should migrate to AVD using the automated process within Nerdio Manager .

items.title: Settings:
items.summary: Update Azure Runbook Modules: Added the ability to update selected or all Azure Runbook modules to their latest version directly from the Scripted Actions settings page, simplifying module maintenance across your environment. View Egress Path Status: Added an Egress Path status to the Linked Networks settings page that displays the identified method used for routing internet traffic for each network, allowing quick identification of any networks still relying on legacy default outbound access.

items.title: REST API:
items.summary: List Linked Mailboxes and WebHooks : Added new endpoints to retrieve a list of linked mailboxes and a list of linked webhooks. Manage Notifications: Added a new endpoint for managing notifications. Enable/Disable Console Connect Regions: Added new endpoints to enable or disable specific Console Connect regions.

items.title: Installer Now Uses Cert-Based Auth:
items.summary: New installations of Nerdio Manager now use certificate-based authentication for App Registrations by default, replacing client secrets with a more secure authentication method.

items.title: Display UPN:
items.summary: The user's UPN is now displayed beneath the display name in the upper-right corner, making it easier to identify the user context of the current session.

items.title: Azure Files Settings Refresh:
items.summary: The Azure Files settings experience has been redesigned with a tabbed layout, making it easier to navigate and manage configurations.

items.title: FSLogix
items.summary: Reset: Changed the default option selected and added a new option, Archive and delete after 30 days , when modifying existing FSLogix profiles.

items.title: Scripted Sequences:
items.summary: Support for Scripted Actions: Existing Scripted Actions (Windows) may now be added as a task within a Scripted Sequence. Changes to the source script are automatically propagated to the sequence. Cross-Tenant Support: AVD and Intune devices located in linked Intune tenants may now have scripted sequences deployed to them, simplifying the management of Intune devices across a distributed management estate. Note Native Intune applications are not supported with Scripted Sequences. Task Worker Enhancements: Task Worker deployment no longer requires individual scripts and groups per device. Pagination has been added to the Scripted Sequences Executions page and all Task Worker Analytics pages. A tasks tab has been added for Task Worker Analytics , providing extensive reporting on the progress of tasks. A refresh button has been added for Task Worker Analytics , allowing data to be updated on demand.

items.title: Unified App Management:
items.summary: Nutanix Support: AVD Hybrid on Nutanix environments now support the deployment of applications via policies and ad hoc using the session host context menu. ShellApps Cache Efficiency: The ShellApps cache is now cleared on target desktops on a 7-day rolling schedule to avoid potential storage issues. Search by Application IDs: Application IDs can now be searched for and selected when creating application groups.

items.title: Real Time Insights:
items.summary: Auto-update Support for Insights Worker: Nerdio Manager now supports auto-update of the Insights Worker (on-device script that collects and sends data used for Real-Time Insights). As the NME version updates, a backend process will automatically update all endpoints with the latest worker. Configurable Log Directory: Added support for a configurable log data directory.

items.title: Nerdio Modeler Now Supports GPU SKUs:
items.summary: Administrators and prospects can now select a GPU workload type in the Modeler (in-product and online) that surfaces GPU-enabled Azure VM SKUs as the recommended compute options, with contextual guidance on image and driver requirements.

items.title: Intune Insights App Metering (Private Preview):
items.summary: Introduced a new App Metering feature that allows administrators to review the true usage of applications for in-scope devices within their organization. Review metrics on a per-application basis and drill down into usage details to identify unused applications for license reclamation.

items.title: Intune Insights OS and Patch Status showing as ‘Unknown’:
items.summary: Devices may fail to report the OS and patch versions correctly, resulting in an unknown status being displayed. This is planned for resolution.

items.title: Azure Files "Smart" Blob access tier:
items.summary: Azure Files storage accounts with the "Smart" blob access tier set as the default will not appear in Nerdio Manager. We will support this access tier in an upcoming release.

items.title: Console Connect Regions:
items.summary: Enabling or changing Console Connect regions may result in an error in the 8.0 Public Preview release. Previous versions are not impacted. This will be resolved in the upcoming GA release.

items.title: Removed ability to migrate to different resource group:
items.summary: The option to move a VM to a different Azure resource group during AVD migration has been removed due to resource group lock conflicts affecting both source and destination groups. This feature is being refactored and will be re-introduced in a future release.

items.title: AVD Hybrid on VMware vSphere
items.summary: support is now available in Public Preview! Learn more... AVD HYBRID ON VMWARE VSPHERE What is the feature? AVD Hybrid on VMware vSphere lets you run Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts on your own VMware vSphere infrastructure. Session host VMs are managed through vCenter Server and connected to Azure through Azure Arc. What does it do for me? You manage vSphere session hosts from Nerdio Manager, alongside your Azure, Azure Local and Nutanix host pools. Nerdio Manager can add, delete, start, stop, restart, resize and re-image session hosts, and supports auto-scale, scripted actions, Real-Time Insights, Console Connect and application management. How do I configure and use it? Link vCenter Server from System > Settings > Integrations > vSphere , configure the Hybrid Client App, and then create a hybrid host pool with Add vSphere host pool . You need vCenter Server 8.0 Update 3, ESXi 8.0, a VM template with VMware Tools installed, and a session host network that provides DHCP. vSphere host pools use Active Directory join. Further reading: AVD Hybrid on VMware vSphere AVD Hybrid on VMware vSphere: Create a VM template Create a Custom Role for Nerdio Manager in vCenter Server AVD Hybrid on VMware vSphere: Enable dynamic host pool Auto-scaling AVD Hybrid on VMware vSphere: Enable personal host pool Auto-scaling

items.title: Windows 365 License Management
items.summary: is now available in Public Preview. This feature enables admins to view, assign, and unassign Windows 365 licenses directly via Nerdio Manager. Learn more... WINDOWS 365 LICENSE MANAGEMENT What is the feature? A Windows 365 page that shows the assigned and purchased quantity of every Windows 365 Enterprise and Flex license in your tenant. What does it do for me? You can assign Enterprise licenses to users directly or through an Entra ID group, unassign them, and see which licenses each user holds. Every change runs as a task, so you keep a history. How do I configure and use it? In the Intune integration, set Windows 365 to Manage, and set Windows 365 license management to Read-only or Manage. To add or remove members of license groups, also set Group membership to Manage. Grant admin consent if Nerdio Manager asks for new Microsoft Graph permissions. Then go to Cloud Desktops > Windows 365 > License Management . Further reading: Windows 365: License Management

items.title: Remote Support
items.summary: Our new  feature (self-hosted alternative to Console Connect) is now available in Private Preview. If you are interested in trying Remote Support, please request access here: Nerdio Remote Support Private Preview Request Learn more... REMOTE SUPPORT What is the feature? Remote Support is a self-hosted alternative to Console Connect. The server, database and logs run in your own Azure subscription, and Nerdio Manager deploys them for you with one Enable action. What does it do for me? Support staff can open a Toolbox session (unattended, with a terminal, file transfer, logs and power controls) or an Interactive user session (remote control) on AVD session hosts, Windows 365 Cloud PCs and Intune-managed Windows devices. Nerdio Manager roles control access, so operators do not need separate accounts. Console Connect remains fully supported. How do I configure and use it? Remote Support is available only where Nerdio has enabled it, so request access with the form linked in this announcement. After it is enabled, go to System > Settings > Nerdio and expand the Remote Support section. Further reading: Remote Support: overview and deployment Remote Support: enable and configure for host pools and devices Remote Support: connect to a device (Toolbox and Interactive sessions)

items.title: Global Pools:
items.summary: Pool Group overrides: Pool Groups can now override the Global Pool's Active Directory, Virtual Machines, RDP, FSLogix, Scripted Actions, and Azure Capacity Extender profiles, and can have their own auto-scale configuration, from the Profiles step when creating a group or the Profiles tab when editing one. Pool Groups inherit profiles from the Global Pool by default; each profile can be overridden independently. Overrides apply only to the host pools in that pool group. Overridden profiles column: The Pool Groups grid now shows an Overridden profiles column that lists the profiles each group overrides. Groups with no overrides show None (all inherited). Workspace at the pool group level: The workspace is now selected once at the pool group level instead of each time a host pool is created, and a workspace can be created from the pool group creation screen. RemoteApp import and export: Global Pools now support RemoteApp import and export functionality. Permissions for Global Pool creation and management: Nerdio Manager now checks for the Microsoft Graph permissions Group.ReadWrite.All and GroupMember.ReadWrite.All on the Global Pools overview page and when you create a Global Pool. If either permission is missing, you can grant it from the same page. Assignment policy defaults: The Percentage option now appears second in the distribution mode selector, and Attribute is the default for new assignment policies. Tooltips and labels: Added tooltips throughout Global Pools and clarified the labels under “Burst beyond base capacity percent”.

items.title: Host pools:
items.summary: Regional host pools: Workspaces and their host pools can now be created with the "Regional" deployment scope for supported regions. More details here Custom views: A custom view can now contain both static and dynamic host pools. Host pool profile hibernation: You can now create a profile with the hibernation option enabled. Hibernation is not used if the host pool type or settings do not support it.

items.title: Auto-scale:
items.summary: Power management-only mode: A new Power management auto-scale method has been added that starts and stops existing session hosts only, and never creates, deletes, or re-images them. This is for organizations with strict change-control requirements. Base and Burst capacity must be 0 when it is enabled, and both the default and alternative schedules must use the same method. It is not available for personal host pools. The method is also available in the REST API through the "autoScaleMethod" field. Auto-shrink timer reset setting: A new "Reset auto-shrink timer" option in the auto-shrink section of the auto-scale configuration allows you to choose what events reset a desktop's auto-shrink timer. Time zone selector: A time zone selector is now available on the auto-scale history page, so you can view activity in a chosen time zone when reviewing auto-scale history. Back button on auto-scale history: The auto-scale history page now has a Back button that returns you to the previous page.

items.title: Azure Capacity Extender:
items.summary: Availability zone failover for single SKU: Session hosts can now automatically fail over to a different availability zone using the same VM SKU, so an alternate VM size is no longer required. This supports customers who are limited to a single VM SKU. To use this feature, enable Availability zone awareness in the Azure Capacity Extender profile, and select multiple zones under the “Deploy VMs across availability zones” setting in the Virtual Machines profile. Quota exhaustion handling: Azure Capacity Extender now uses the alternate VM size when the subscription quota for the host pool's VM size is exhausted, not only when Azure has no capacity in the selected region.

items.title: Self-service portal:
items.summary: Connect button: For personal desktop host pools, end users can now launch their desktop from the self-service portal. This is configured by administrators within the host pool settings. End-user pre-staging: End users can now pre-stage their personal session hosts and disks with up to five schedules. When an end user sets a schedule, it replaces the auto-scale profile pre-stage schedules for the host pool. This is configured by administrators within the host pool settings. Administrators may also view the end user's pre-stage schedule from the host pool page. Learn more... SELF-SERVICE PORTAL: CONNECT AND PRE-STAGING What is the feature? Two host pool settings control what end users can do with their personal desktop in the self-service portal: connect to it, and pre-stage it on a schedule. What does it do for me? The Connect button can open the desktop in the Windows App, in a browser, or in either (the user chooses), or you can turn it off. Pre-staging lets end users set up to five schedules. A schedule that a user sets replaces the pre-stage schedules in the host pool's auto-scale profile. How do I configure and use it? Open the host pool's Settings and go to the User Self-Service Portal tab. Use Allow end users to connect to their desktop and Allow end users to PRE-STAGE desktop . Further reading: Personal host pool user self-service

items.title: Storage:
items.summary: Entra ID cloud-only identities for Azure Files: Azure Files shares used for FSLogix profiles now support Microsoft Entra ID cloud-only identities natively, replacing the previous Entra ID-join workaround. Azure Files auto-scale default minimums: The default minimum bandwidth and IOPS values shown when you first configure Azure Files auto-scale will now appear blank so that customers have control of the thresholds when first creating an auto-scale rule. User Profiles page relocated: The FSLogix User Profiles page has moved from Cloud Desktops > Storage > Azure Files to Cloud Desktops > User Profiles > FSLogix. Shares and Tasks remain under the Azure Files page. Azure Files v2 REST API support has been introduced.

items.title: Azure Local:
items.summary: Storage path support for session hosts: You can now select the storage path when deploying session hosts to Azure Local.

items.title: AVD Hybrid for Nutanix:
items.summary: Network overlays (Flow networks): Session hosts can now be deployed and managed on Nutanix Flow overlay networks. OS disk storage container selection: When you create, add or re-image a Nutanix session host, you can now choose the storage container for the OS disk. The list is limited to the cluster of the selected subnet. The selection is optional; if you leave it blank, the OS disk stays on the template's storage. Preserve MAC address on re-image: When a Nutanix session host is re-imaged, the replacement VM keeps the original MAC address, so its DHCP reservation and IP assignment are retained and re-imaging at scale does not require DNS or DHCP changes. Convert a host pool to Nutanix or vSphere: You can now convert a host pool to a Nutanix or vSphere host pool. Force power-off fallback: After a configurable number of failed graceful shutdown attempts, Nutanix session hosts are now powered off forcibly. This applies to auto-scale scale-in and to manual Restart and Stop actions. The fallback is a global Nutanix setting that applies to all linked Prism Central instances, under System > Settings > Integrations > Nutanix > Power operations. It is enabled by default, and the default is 3 failed graceful attempts (about 3 minutes each) before the host is forced off. You can change the number of attempts (1 to 10) or turn the fallback off.

items.title: AVD Hybrid on VMware vSphere (Public Preview):
items.summary: Integration and management: Link VMware vCenter to Nerdio Manager from the Integrations page using a login and password. The Host Pools page supports adding and deleting host pools and managing users, groups, and application groups. The Hosts page supports adding a host. Host operations: Start, stop, restart, resize (CPU, memory, and disk), and re-image session hosts from Nerdio Manager. Auto-scale: Auto-scale is now supported for vSphere host pools. Scripted actions: Deploy scripted actions to vSphere session hosts and desktop images. Session time limits: Session time limit settings are now supported for vSphere session hosts. Real-Time Insights: vSphere host pools can now use Real-Time Insights. Custom views: Custom views now support vSphere host pools and session hosts. Console Connect: Launch a console session on a vSphere session host from Nerdio Manager. Applications: Application management (UAM) is now available for vSphere host pools: vSphere host pools can be targeted in application deployment policies, and apps can be deployed directly to hosts with the Deploy apps menu option. MSIX App Attach and installed application visibility are also supported. Run Script and FSLogix: Run scripts on vSphere session hosts, and use a custom or predefined FSLogix profile in host pool settings.

items.title: Certificate trust verification for hypervisor connections:
items.summary: When you add or edit a connection to an on-premises hypervisor such as Nutanix Prism Central or vCenter, Nerdio Manager now retrieves the endpoint's TLS certificate and shows its details, including issuer, validity, and SHA-256 fingerprint, before saving. Self-signed or untrusted certificates require you to explicitly confirm trust. This replaces the manual Nutanix:DisableSslValidation app setting which can be removed after upgrading to 8.3.

items.title: Remote connections enabled during provisioning:
items.summary: Nerdio Manager now enables remote connections on AVD Hybrid session hosts when it provisions them, so hosts cloned from a template with remote connections disabled can still be connected to. This applies to Nutanix and vSphere. Templates that already have remote connections enabled are unaffected.
